breakdown: Two-panel vertical split on a shared marble background, 1:1-ish crop. Left: young woman with wet, greasy, flattened hair, neutral-to-glum expression — the wrong state. Right: same-role woman with voluminous curled hair holding the cream-white electric spray comb (button and indicator visible) up to her hair — the resolved state with the product as the visible explanation. Argument structure is wrong-state vs answer in one glance, i.e. job=pain, device=split, closest to the --mirror shape because the right side is a person in the corrected state with the product secondary-to-prominent. It deviates from the base skeleton by three softenings that look deliberate for a beauty vertical: no X/check badges, no grayscale on the wrong side, and the product held mid-use. G4 still holds (right side brighter, airier); G5 holds (both photographic, same background and lighting register); G7 holds (hand-held comb in a plausible use moment). Hypothesis for curation: a 'soft/beauty' presentation register where hard judgment marks (badges, grayscale) would cheapen an aesthetic category — one observation, no action until the >=3 evidence threshold. Likely a real listing/ad image of the actual product; useful later as a reference for the product's face, though not a clean packshot.

Single photographic frame, zero graphic overlays, wide-ish crop. A woman in her 30s-40s in pajama bottoms and a t-shirt stands at a bathroom counter looking directly into the lens with drawn brows and a pressed, frustrated mouth — restrained everyday frustration, not theatrical pain. Symptom evidence per the G9 hierarchy: rank 1, the frizzy tangled hair itself; rank 3, the pink comb still in her raised hand as the failed tool; plus one hand pulling a strand. Environment is a lived-in bathroom with toothbrush cup, toothpaste tubes, towels and plants — real clutter signaling a disrupted morning routine. A mirror behind her shows her from the back, doubling the symptom evidence exactly as the optional [MIRROR] slot prescribes. Light is even, bright, flat daylight; palette desaturated neutrals; no red anywhere; nothing signals advertising and no product is present. This is a clean match for 01-pain-scene --confront with every v1.1 slot satisfied — it appears to be the very seed exemplar that produced the --confront variant (seed conversation.md), now formally ledgered as its first evidence. Rendering style suggests it is itself AI-generated, which does not affect its value as a structural exemplar.

breakdown: 3D technical see-through render of the electric spray comb itself: translucent shell revealing a labeled Li-ion battery in the handle, a PCB with chip and colored wiring, and the atomizer module in the head shown actively emitting a stream of mist particles; massage bristles visible under the head. Argument structure: job=mechanism (justify capability by what is inside the OBJECT — battery capacity, chip control, atomizer), device=xray (reserved in vocabulary, first exemplar). No comparison, no person, no symptom — it exhibits rather than argues, sitting on the step-3 tier beside ghostbody (inside the body) and spec-split (component combat). Blue/cyan dominance reads as correct-mechanism under G3; the copper-orange traces are decorative but sit in tension with G3's orange=wrong-pressure if reused as signal. In-image text present (spec label) — a claim and a model-weakness both; the library version of this type must externalize numbers. G7 exempt (technical render register). Likely sourced from the product's own listing gallery.

deviations.observed: no person as subject — only a wary hand entering frame; the indicted OBJECT (old wall outlet with exposed tangled wires) is the protagonist

breakdown: Single photographic frame, zero graphic overlays: an old grimy wall outlet plate hanging open, a disassembled socket dangling on red/blue/yellow tangled wires, warm low-key directional light raking the dirty wall, a bare hand reaching in hesitantly from frame left. The argument is not 'recognize your felt pain' (no person, no symptom on a body) but 'look at what the old way actually involves' — indicting an object in daily life, which is job=cause, delivered through the documentary scene device (job cause + device scene has no existing type; 02-cause-anatomy is its illustrated sibling). G9 logic transfers: the hazard is physical fact in frame, the hand carries hesitation, no red signal graphics needed — the exposed copper does the work. Low-key cinematic grade, lived-in grime, nothing staged-looking; G7 passes (a mid-repair moment anyone recognizes). Fits the advertorial 'old way' beat before a no-wiring product answer. First exemplar for candidate 02-cause-scene. Product domain context: mist air cooler funnel (traditional AC installation pain).

deviations.observed: invisible force (electrical arc/interference) visualized as a bright teal glowing arc with concentric rings and purple sparks composited over a photographic wall cavity — a graphic-FX layer on a real scene; no existing device covers this (flagged: new device value `aura` would need a vocabulary gate)

breakdown: Photographic base: a rough rectangular cavity cut into a plaster wall, copper pipes and teal-sheathed cables converging into it from all sides. Over it, a heavy stylized FX layer: a bright teal electric arc bridging two conductors, concentric glowing rings radiating from the contact point, purple spark filaments. The argument: make the INVISIBLE danger inside your walls visible — job=cause (indicting hidden electrical risk of the old installation path), but the device is neither scene (which bans overlays) nor anatomy (2D illustration) nor xray (see-through product); it is an effect-visualization layer over a real photo. Proposed as 02-cause-aura with the new device value flagged for the vocabulary gate — per governance this record accumulates evidence and changes nothing until reviewed. G3 tension: teal/cyan is used here for DANGER, colliding with blue=correct in the library palette — any adopted skeleton must flip the hazard color to red/orange. One exemplar; the aesthetic skews dramatic and may read as fearmongering on marketplace channels — advertorial-leaning. Product domain: mist air cooler funnel.

Second exemplar for candidate 02-cause-scene (same structure as the exposed-outlet image: object-as-protagonist, person absent or partial, documentary register, no signal colors). Note the handwritten text here is diegetic (part of the photographed object), which sits outside the G6 text ban's intent (overlay text) — a scoping question to settle if this candidate is drafted: diegetic text allowed, overlay text banned. Candidate now at 2 distinct exemplars. Product domain: mist air cooler funnel (old-wiring hassle narrative).

deviations.observed: confront gaze paired with low-key candid lighting (single bare bulb in a dark basement) — the current variants hard-bundle gaze with light (candid=low-key, confront=daylight); this exemplar crosses the pair, evidence the two axes can decouple

breakdown: Single cinematic frame, no overlays: a man in his 50s crouches in a dark basement beside two aged breaker panels, a single bare bulb overhead, pipes and joists in shadow. His face is turned to the lens with a drained, troubled expression — restrained, not theatrical — landing this as gaze=confront. Symptom evidence per G9: the environment itself is the evidence (old panels, sticker-covered doors, bare-bulb infrastructure), rank-1 on-object condition; his posture (elbow on knee, hand slack) carries resignation. Low-key warm key from the bulb, deep shadow across most of the frame, desaturated amber-grey grade, film-still character — everything else matches 01-pain-scene cleanly. The one structural surprise is the gaze/light pairing: current variant definitions bundle confront with flat daylight, but this image demonstrates confront+low-key working (the basement is where the problem lives; daylight would be false). Logged as a deviation for the >=2/3 rule — if it recurs, the patch is to decouple gaze and light into independent axes rather than variant bundles. G7 passes; no red, no product. Product domain: mist air cooler funnel.

Diegetic screen digits present in both insets. G7 tension: the floating packshot is a sanctioned graphic layer; the doctor scene itself passes. Product domain: wrist blood pressure monitor.
